> Curated papers, systems, and datasets for Text-to-SQL that can recognize ambiguity, ask useful questions, and decline unsupported requests.

Natural-language questions do not always determine one SQL query, and a database cannot answer every request. This collection focuses on how NL2SQL agents detect these situations, resolve them through interaction or additional evidence, and evaluate when to answer or abstain.

[**Explore the interactive catalog →**](https://duyvuleo.github.io/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/) · [Browse papers](papers/README.md) · [Compare benchmarks](docs/benchmark-matrix.md) · [Try the examples](examples/README.md) · [Contribute](CONTRIBUTING.md)

Updated **2026-11-24**. Each paper includes a concise summary, publication status, public sources, and a verification date. Core work and adjacent methods are marked separately. Resource counts include clearly labeled benchmark designs whose artifacts are not yet verified released.

[**Read the detailed paper notes →**](papers/reading-notes.md) for methods, evaluation conditions, findings, limitations and checks against the original text. The index records completed readings and remaining access gaps.

## Scope

We include work that directly studies ambiguity, underspecification, answerability, clarification, or abstention in natural-language querying of relational databases. We also include selected verification, uncertainty, and contextual-grounding methods when their relevance to those problems is explicit. Generic SQL-generation systems and broad agent frameworks belong in the related collections unless they provide a concrete capability relevant to this scope.

An ambiguous request, an unsupported request, a model error, and a valid query returning no rows are different cases. Likewise, a publication, an announced repository, released artifacts, and independently reproduced results are different kinds of evidence. The annotations preserve these distinctions; inclusion is not a deployment endorsement.

## Recent additions

| Year | Paper / venue | Concise summary | Links |

| 2026 | [AskWise: Execution-Guided Clarification of Intent and Data in Text-to-SQL](papers/README.md#askwise)<br>arXiv preprint<br><em>core</em> | AskWise pairs query interpretations with possible database repairs, asks about choices supported by execution witnesses, and returns an answer when all surviving worlds agree. A four-cell bound selects EC2-maximizing questions for uniform binary worlds with Boolean answers. Synthetic policy experiments and an AmbiQT value-swap study expose the limits of grouping queries by observed results alone. Correctness requires the true query/data world to be included and replies to be truthful; the model study measures reference-signature retention, not end-to-end dialogue success. | [Code](https://github.com/fmh1art/AskWise)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#askwise)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/askwise.md) |
| 2026 | [Know Your Context Bank: Repairing Inconsistency and Measuring Generalization in Context-Aware Text-to-SQL](papers/README.md#context-bank)<br>arXiv preprint<br><em>adjacent</em> | Audits SQL example banks using semantic-unit comparisons, a distilled conflict scorer and two-track adjudication under explicit conventions. Cleaning improves one-model fine-tuning, while separate convention-open experiments show that inconsistent examples can steer otherwise defensible answers. CAT-BIRD and CAT-Spider measure transfer across scored distances from a context bank. LLM labels, selected difficulty, simple retrieval and single-seed runs limit generalization claims; clarification and abstention are not evaluated. | Release not verified<br>[Details](papers/README.md#context-bank)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/context-bank.md) |
| 2026 | [Leveraging Query Optimizers to Verify the Soundness of LLM-based Query Rewrites for Real-World Workloads, and More!](papers/README.md#qo-verify)<br>CIDR 2026<br><em>adjacent</em> | QO-Verify checks whether two SQL queries share a logical expression in optimizer-generated memos. SQL Server experiments verify a subset of LLM rewrites, with coverage depending on available transformation rules and search limits. Soundness relies on those rules and correct expression matching; Unknown is inconclusive. The method preserves an input SQL query rather than verifying its alignment with a natural-language request. | Release not verified<br>[Details](papers/README.md#qo-verify)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/qo-verify.md) |
| 2026 | [PV-SQL: Synergizing Database Probing and Rule-based Verification for Text-to-SQL Agents](papers/README.md#pv-sql)<br>Findings of ACL 2026<br><em>adjacent</em> | Combines targeted database probes with a rule-based checklist and iterative SQL repair. Development-set ablations on BIRD, Mini-Dev and Spider support the contribution of probing and repair, but construct checks do not certify intended semantics. Reported component success measures constraint satisfaction rather than whole-query correctness, and public source checks differ from the paper description. Clarification and unanswerability are not evaluated. | [Code](https://github.com/magic-YuanTian/PV-SQL)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#pv-sql)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/pv-sql.md) |
| 2026 | [A Model of Diverse Sampling from Language Models](papers/README.md#pooldpp)<br>NeurIPS 2026 (official program listing; arXiv version reviewed)<br><em>adjacent</em> | PoolDPP selects sets of candidate strings using likelihood-weighted determinantal diversity, with stochastic sampling and greedy MAP variants. An AMBROSIA experiment measures coverage of annotated SQL interpretations and full-result precision. Reported recall gains over ancestral sampling trade off precision; question-paired tests do not resolve gains over K-means. Coverage is limited by the generated pool, and embedding diversity does not certify semantic validity or identify the user&#x27;s intended reading. | [Code](https://github.com/rycolab/pool-dpp)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#pooldpp)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/pooldpp.md) |

Reports 153 failures among 236 retained intents and additional BIRD analyses. Counts are conditional on executable cases; proposed clarification/repair responses are not tested. The later VSL evaluation reuses a selected subset of this corpus. | Release not verified<br>[Details](papers/README.md#operationalization-failures)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/operationalization-failures.md) |
| 2026 | [Two Surfaces of Ambiguity: Complementary Detection for Text-to-SQL](papers/README.md#two-surfaces)<br>AIDB workshop at VLDB 2026<br><em>core</em> | Combines question introspection with sampled-SQL differences to broaden clarification coverage on BIRD-Interact. Its union improves detection but does not significantly outperform introspection alone on downstream task success; AMBROSIA interpretation coverage improves while precision falls. Simulator-label limitations, question budgets and unexecuted detection probes constrain interpretation. Public pipelines reuse existing benchmarks and require separate inputs. | [Code](https://github.com/BHT-Math/text2sql-ambiguity-detection)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#two-surfaces)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/two-surfaces.md) |
| 2026 | [Text-to-(Single-or-Multi)-SQL: Bridging Real-World Needs with Spider𝕊](papers/README.md#spiders)<br>Findings of EMNLP 2026; pages 9792–9821<br><em>adjacent</em> | Studies evaluation of clear composite requests answered by one or several SQL queries. Its proposed score permits extra columns, rejects extra rows and matches predicted result units one-to-one against a gold solution set. This addresses reference-format false negatives, not competing meanings or unanswerability. Single-instance matching, inconsistent strategy/prompt wording and unverified artifact access limit conclusions. | Release not verified<br>[Details](papers/README.md#spiders)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/spiders.md) |

## Contributing

Suggest a resource or correction through an [issue](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/issues/new/choose) or pull request. Include a primary source and explain the connection to ambiguity or unanswerability. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the entry format and checks.

The canonical records are [papers.json](data/papers.json) and [resources.json](data/resources.json). The indexes are generated, so contributors only need to maintain one record per work.
